reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) shows dynamic precipitation and recrystallization in a single-phase FCC HEA, not at FCC/BCC phase boundaries, and E2 indicates recrystallization can increase creep rate via grain boundary sliding, contradicting the premise that grain refinement always enhances creep resistance. The transferability to a dual-phase coating is unsupported.
premises: Dynamic precipitation at phase boundaries impedes dislocation motion
Dynamic recrystallization refines grain size during creep
Combined precipitation and recrystallization increase creep activation energy
Stress-assisted dislocation climb is the rate-controlling creep mechanism
The cited CoCrFeNiMn HEA behavior is directly transferable to an FCC/BCC coating
